To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a publish/subscribe server can reduce its load and improve scalability if it is allowed to off-load some of its subscription processing to the network, and (2) the network can reduce its load if the publish/subscribe server off-loads only those subscription processing tasks that it can off-load without affecting the quality of the system.

(i) the interface between the database system and the network can significantly affect the system performance; (ii) by carefully designing the interface, we can significantly reduce the server-side processing cost and the network load; (iii) the interface design should be based on the characteristics of the queries; and (iv) we have developed a general framework for the design and evaluation of the interface between the publish/subscribe system and the network.

(i) it is possible to build a scalable publish/subscribe system by exploiting the query semantic and the interface between the database system and the network; and (ii) by exploiting the query sematics and building an appropriate interace between the database system, it is possible for the system to achieve orders-of magnitude savings in network traffice and low server side processing cost.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interface between the database system and the publish/subscribe network.
the design of a publish/subscribe interface between the database system and the network.
the design and analysis of a publish/subscribe interface between a database system and a network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the database and network communities have been working independently for years, but the time is right for a new generation of publish/subscribe systems to emerge that exploit both database-side and networking-side capabilities to achieve better performance and scalability.

the interface between the database side and the network side is an important component of a publish/subscribe systems and should be designed with careful consideration of both the database side and network side.

the database/network interface is an important component of a large-scale publish/ subscribe system, and that a well-designed interface between these two components can significantly improve the overall system performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

by exploiting the semantics of the queries in a publish/subscribe database system and building an appropriate database/network interface, it is possible for the database to achieve orders-ofmagnitude savings in network traffic, while at the same time, maintaining a low server-side cost.

the interface between database and network is a crucial component of publish/subscribe systems, and that it is essential to design and optimize this component in a way that is sensitive to both the database and network characteristics.
the interface between a database server and the underlying network is critical in large-scale publish /subscribe systems and should not be overlooked.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to build a scalable publish/subscribe infrastructure that is both efficient and expressive.

the design of the database/network interface is critical to the performance of a publish/subscribe systems, and that the database and the networking communities should work together in order to achieve the best possible performance.
a careful interface design can lead to substantial performance improvements in publish/subscribe systems, even in the presence of a complex and diverse set of queries.
